title: phoradendron tomentosum
intro: Phoradendron tomentosum, commonly known as the Poison Ivy of the West, is a flowering plant in the mistletoe family, known for its highly toxic and irritating sap. The sap of Phoradendron tomentosum has been used in traditional medicine to treat various ailments, including fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, due to its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties. The therapeutic actions of Phoradendron tomentosum are attributed to its ability to stimulate the immune system, reduce pain and inflammation, and promote wound healing. The bioactive constituents of Phoradendron tomentosum include diterpenes, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
